title: Analytic Coherence and the Dirac Equation Fourth (DE4): A Unified Framework for Smoothness, Existence, and Collective Dynamics
content: Nature displays an enduring tendency toward smoothness — from the self-consistent coherence of quantum fields to the ordered morphology of galaxies. This paper introduces an analytic framework, termed the Dirac Equation Fourth (DE4), which unifies these manifestations under a common differential constraint. DE4 is expressed as a relation between a collective field potential Λ and its curvature Φ, where the balance of spatial and temporal derivatives enforces bounded, differentiable behavior across interacting domains. In contrast to traditional field formulations, which impose smoothness as an assumption, DE4 treats smoothness as an emergent consequence of analytic coupling. The paper derives DE4 in full form, demonstrates its operation in a three-body collective example, and connects its eigenvalue structure to established results in harmonic analysis and density functional theory. The addition of a complex analytic term extends the framework into a higher-dimensional field space, introducing a built-in smoothing mechanism comparable to Cauchy–Riemann conditions. This construction yields bounded field solutions without requiring external regularization, offering parallels to the existence and smoothness properties sought in Navier–Stokes and related nonlinear systems. Applications span from multi-body dynamics to field-theoretic coherence and data regularization. By consolidating analytic, numerical, and conceptual threads into a single coherent presentation, the hybrid DE4 framework provides a new way of understanding why smoothness, rather than singularity, dominates the observable universe. The work closes with an outlook toward computational implementations and interdisciplinary extensions that link analytic coherence with physical stability and informational integrity.
